verdict.rationale: Navan documents its own expense-management pieces relevant to coding spend: receipt scanning, custom company fields with managed option values, accounting and ERP settings, per-transaction activity history, ERP integrations, and real-time spend data that can be broken down by vendor or category. The evidence does not show that transactions are automatically coded at the point of spend with merchant, category, memo and receipt attached, so the 'coded as it happens' core is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit real-time or automatic transaction coding at swipe, documented memo capture, receipt matching to card transactions, a month-end close or review workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, spend is coded as it happens — merchant, category, memo, receipt — so month-end close is a review, not an archaeology dig
